finding.claim: decode(subject=...) does not enforce subject binding when the token has no sub claim; a validly signed token without sub passes the subject check.
finding.source: Attacker holds a validly signed token from the same key that has no sub claim (e.g. refresh, service or anonymous token type from the same issuer). Precondition: application relies on subject= for authorization.

trace.note: If 'sub' not in payload, return without comparing against subject.
Comparison to subject only happens when sub is present.
require defaults to [], so sub presence is not enforced.

finding.guards_checked: Signature verified (api_jws.py:269-277, 368-417); algorithm allow-list enforced (api_jws.py:386-387); exp/nbf/iat/iss/aud enforced; _validate_iss (api_jwt.py:571-572) and _validate_aud (api_jwt.py:529-532) raise MissingRequiredClaimError when their claim is absent, so the sub handling is inconsistent with them. Verdict PLAUSIBLE, medium-low: depends on the application using subject= for authorization and the same key signing tokens without sub.

finding.claim: HMACAlgorithm.prepare_key accepts DER-encoded RSA/EC public key bytes as an HMAC secret, enabling algorithm-confusion forgery when HS* and asymmetric algorithms are both allowed.
finding.source: Attacker knows the public key (public by definition). Precondition: application passes the public key as raw DER bytes (not PEM or SSH) and allow-lists HS256 alongside RS256/ES256, e.g. algorithms=['HS256','RS256'].
finding.sink: HMAC signature verification of the attacker-forged token.

trace.note: decode_complete: algorithms non-empty, so the call is permitted.
alg='HS256' is in the caller's allow-list.
get_algorithm_by_name returns HMACAlgorithm; prepare_key(key) is called.
force_bytes and empty-key check pass for DER bytes.
is_pem_format is False for DER; is_ssh_key (utils.py:141-142) is also False.
JWK-shaped check does not apply to DER bytes; key returned as raw secret.
HMAC verify over signing input with the DER bytes; forged HS256 token verifies.

finding.guards_checked: Algorithm allow-list is enforced but permits HS256 by configuration; PEM guard (utils.py:126-127) and SSH guard (utils.py:141-142) do not match DER; JWK guard (algorithms.py:344-355) does not match DER; compare_digest (algorithms.py:411) is constant-time but irrelevant to the forgery; docstring warns against mixing HS* with RS*/ES* (api_jwt.py:213-217). PEM and JWK inputs are rejected, so default PEM usage is not affected. Verdict PLAUSIBLE, low-medium: requires DER key bytes plus mixed algorithms.

finding.claim: get_signing_key_from_jwt forces an outbound JWKS fetch for every unknown or missing kid, bypassing the 5-minute JWK-set cache and enabling request amplification against the IdP.
finding.source: Unauthenticated attacker sends tokens with random or missing kid. Precondition: application calls PyJWKClient.get_signing_key_from_jwt on untrusted input.
finding.sink: Outbound HTTP request to the JWKS endpoint (urllib urlopen) on each refresh=True lookup.

trace.note: kid read from the unverified token header.
match_kid against cached keys finds no match.
get_jwk_set calls fetch_data when data is None.
urlopen performs an outbound request for each attacker token.
Lookup still fails and raises PyJWKClientError; lru_cache (lines 100-104) does not cache exceptions, so misses re-fetch too.

finding.guards_checked: URI fixed at construction and restricted to http/https (jwks_client.py:77-82), so this is not SSRF; only successful fetches update the cache (jwks_client.py:129-134); no rate limit or negative cache exists. Verdict PLAUSIBLE, low: amplification/availability issue largely consistent with the documented refresh-on-miss design.
